newsitem.title: USA: Holbrooke to see Cypriot leaders before U.N. talks.
newsitem.headline: Holbrooke to see Cypriot leaders before U.N. talks.

text.p: U.S. mediator Richard Holbrooke will meet the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities in New York on Tuesday before they attend U.N.-sponsored talks, Holbrooke's office said on Wednesday.

Holbrooke, appointed by President Bill Clinton to lead a U.S. drive for a settlement on the divided Mediterranean island, will meet Greek Cypriot leader Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash separately.
"The purpose will be to get acquainted and lay the groundwork for negotiations that will get rolling in the fall," an official in Holbrooke's office said in a telephone interview.
Holbrooke, who now works for a bank in New York, is a long-time former State Department official who mediated the 1995 Dayton Peace talks that ended the war in Bosnia.
The U.N. talks are to be opened by Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Wednesday at Troutbeck, a rural resort 90 miles (145 km) north of New York, and continue until July 13.

It will be the first face-to-face meeting in nearly three years between Clerides, president of the internationally recognised Greek Cypriot-led government in Nicosia, and Denktash, who heads a Turkish Cypriot state recognised only by Turkey.

The aim is to revive stalled negotiations on reuniting the island under a bi-communal, bi-zonal federation. Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkish troops took over the north after a coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.
